title: Projects: creation, quotas, labels and life cycle

videos.script: Creating a project takes four decisions. Only one of them is forever. {{four}} The id. It is unique across all of Google Cloud, and it is never handed out again, not even after the project is gone. So choose one that will stay true. {{id}} You will make the provider refuse a bad id, and a bad name, before any request exists. {{refuse}} Then, the APIs. A new project has almost all of them switched off. That is a nuisance, and it is also a guardrail. {{apis}} Next come labels. A label is a key and a value, and its job is to be counted. The bill reads them. Finance reads them. {{labels}} Your lab will check the rules for you, and it will show you where the emulator stops. {{gap}} Last, the end of a project's life. Deleting one starts a thirty-day clock. Until it runs out, the project can come back. {{clock}} After that, nothing can bring it back. {{end}}
